Remember one sentence: the designer draws "what he imagined", and the jewelry processing staff turns it into "something that can be worn on the body" - from the metal material to the finished product, every process is in their hands.

This role does not suit careless people who dislike precision work. Jewelry making allows little room for error: a crooked stone setting could ruin the entire piece. Materials are expensive, so impatience quickly becomes costly.

Common paths are: Entrance to jewelry/arts and crafts vocational schools or apprenticeships → Start with basic processes such as polishing and molding → Learn inlays, wax carvings, and welding from masters → Obtain vocational skills related to jewelry processing → Gradually receive custom orders independently or enter high-end workshops.

Suitable for people with steady hands, fine eyesight and the ability to sit still. A one-millimeter diamond has to be embedded into the claw position, and a large area of ​​​​the nail cap is carved. If you don’t have the patience and steady hand shape, you will be discouraged from the first step.

Jewelers And Precious Stone And Metal Workers are engaged in the cutting, shaping, welding, setting, polishing and engraving of precious metal jewelry. They are also responsible for the inspection, grading and setting of gemstones. They are the core craftsmen who turn design drawings into physical jewelry.

paragraphs: The main theme of the day is "see-do-check": first check the order and materials, check the clarity and cracks of the bare stone under a magnifying glass, and then go to the workbench: mold making, welding, stone setting, and polishing follow the process; customized orders need to be tried on and adjusted repeatedly, and finally quality inspection and maintenance are explained to the customers. It's a lot of work on my hands, and my eyes and waist are tired, but the moment the finished product comes out it's worth it.
